issues.problem: Ordering item item_kano_var text reads 'Kano has notable delivery-time variability across all three cities', which is ambiguous — it sounds like Kano's variability extends across all three cities rather than being the most variable of the three. Additionally, the ds_city_delivery_summary shows both Kano and Lagos have variability_rank = 'medium', so Kano does not uniquely have the highest variability.
issues.required_fix: Reword to 'Kano has the most variable delivery times of the three cities' or 'Delivery-time variability is highest in Kano among the three cities'. Alternatively, if the data doesn't support Kano being uniquely most variable, reword to 'Kano's delivery-time variability is notable but not directly relevant to the Lagos staffing decision.'

issues.problem: Screens consistently say '10% lift' (matching glossary teaching blocks) while interactions say '9.8% lift' (matching registry data). The glossary rounds to 10%; the data is 9.8%. This inconsistency between screens and interactions could confuse a learner who reads both.
issues.required_fix: Align on one figure. Either change screens to '9.8% lift' to match the data and interactions, or change interactions to 'roughly 10% lift' / 'about 10% lift' to match the screens and glossary. The glossary itself uses '10% lift' so the simplest fix is to add 'roughly' or 'about' in the screens.
